# MM-P3-L1-HP01-S1 — Lubrication and fluids - Hot Forge hydraulic forging press #1

Revision: Rev C  
Plant: P3, line P3-L1  
Equipment: EQ-P3-L1-HP01

Scope
This document specifies lubrication and hydraulic fluid maintenance for Hot Forge hydraulic forging press EQ-P3-L1-HP01. It defines the required hydraulic oil change interval and the approved lubricant part number, outlines required tools, presents the maintenance procedure with rationale, and states acceptance criteria. This procedure supports safe, reliable operation and is supplemental to general maintenance practices in MM-P3-L1-HP01 and to operational wet checks in SOP-P3-L1-02 and SOP-P3-L1-03.

Background and rationale
Hydraulic fluid condition directly affects system responsiveness, component wear, and contamination control. The specified oil change interval and approved lubricant are selected to balance component life, fluid cleanliness, and operational cost for the press duty profile. Adherence to this procedure keeps contamination levels within machine design limits and reduces the risk of unplanned stoppages and damage to valves, pumps, and cylinders. Records from planned changes inform trending for future optimization.

Specified values
- The hydraulic oil change interval for Hot Forge hydraulic forging press #1 (EQ-P3-L1-HP01) is 2425 hours.
- The lubricant part number for Hot Forge hydraulic forging press #1 (EQ-P3-L1-HP01) is CFW-LUB-927.

Tools and materials
- Approved lubricant: CFW-LUB-927 (use only this part number for top-up or full change).
- Clean, lint-free containers and funnels compatible with the lubricant.
- Particle contamination test kit and fluid sample bottles per MM-P3-L1-HP01.
- Portable vacuum transfer pump or manufacturer-approved drain and fill equipment.
- Clean rags, suitable drip trays, and containment to prevent plant floor contamination.
- Personal protective equipment appropriate for handling hydraulic oil and cleaning agents.
- Record forms or electronic entry prepared as per MM-P3-L1-HP01 and SOP-P3-L1-02.

Procedure
Prepare machine and area
- Place appropriate signage and isolate press from operation following lockout-tagout procedures referenced in MM-P3-L1-HP01. Ensure the area under the reservoir and all drip points is protected with drip trays and absorbent material. Purging or flushing activities must minimize airborne contamination; ensure ventilation as required by site practice.

Obtain fluid sample
- Before any fluid change, take a representative sample from the reservoir using the sample bottle and sampling method in MM-P3-L1-01. Label the sample with equipment id EQ-P3-L1-HP01 and current operating hours. Use the particle contamination test kit and record results. Retain the sample for the equipment maintenance record.

Drain and capture used fluid
- Place a clean container to capture drained fluid. Use the vacuum transfer pump or approved drain method to remove fluid from the reservoir until the reservoir level is below the sump where contamination accumulates. Capture all used fluid in sealed containers for proper disposal according to plant environmental procedures. Clean the reservoir interior with lint-free rags to remove varnish and sediment; collect and dispose of waste rags per plant policy.

Inspect and clean ancillary components
- With the reservoir open, inspect suction screens, return lines, and visible hose ends for debris. Replace or clean filters and strainers per MM-P3-L1-HP01. If particle contamination exceeds limits cited in MM-P3-L1-01, escalate for corrective action and note this in the maintenance record.

Refill with approved lubricant
- Using only CFW-LUB-927, refill to the reservoir fill level prescribed in manufacturer documentation and MM-P3-L1-HP01. Use a clean funnel and sealed lubricant containers to prevent contamination. When topping or filling, ensure the lubricant source is clean and within acceptable condition.

Bleed and operate
- After refill, purge any trapped air following manufacturer guidance and confirm hydraulic system returns to normal operating conditions per SOP-P3-L1-02 and SOP-P3-L1-03. Monitor for unusual noise, temperature rise, or leaks during initial operation and log observations.

Sampling post-change
- After the system has run long enough for the fluid to circulate, take a post-change sample for particle analysis. Record results and place the sample with prior samples as required by MM-P3-L1-01.

Records and documentation
- Complete the maintenance record entry for EQ-P3-L1-HP01 in the equipment history log. Record the operating hours at change, the lubricant part number CFW-LUB-927, particle counts before and after change, and any anomalies found. Attach the sample labels and contamination test results. File a copy per MM-P3-L1-01.

Procedure rationale and examples
- The pre-change sample establishes baseline contamination and helps determine if additional system flushing is required. The post-change sample verifies that contamination levels returned to acceptable ranges and that filters are performing. Using only the approved part number CFW-LUB-927 avoids fluid incompatibility that can cause varnish, seal swelling, or additive depletion. The capture and disposal steps prevent plant contamination and preserve environmental compliance.

Acceptance criteria
- Reservoir refill completed with lubricant part number CFW-LUB-927 documented in the maintenance record.
- Pre-change and post-change particle contamination results recorded and retained per MM-P3-L1-01.
- No visible contamination or residue remaining in the reservoir; suction screens and strainers clean to the extent accessible.
- System operates normally after restart with no abnormal noises, leaks, or functional degradation observed in the period immediately following the change; observations documented and cross-referenced with SOP-P3-L1-02 and SOP-P3-L1-03.
- The hydraulic oil change interval for Hot Forge hydraulic forging press #1 (EQ-P3-L1-HP01) is 2425 hours and is recorded in the equipment maintenance schedule.

Records to keep
- Completed maintenance record for EQ-P3-L1-HP01 including lubricant part number CFW-LUB-927 and oil change hour reading.
- Pre- and post-change fluid sample labels and contamination test results.
- Disposal manifests or waste documentation for removed fluid as required by plant environmental procedures.
- Any corrective actions taken if contamination or component issues were identified.

Related documents
- See MM-P3-L1-HP01 for system-level maintenance policies.
- Refer to SOP-P3-L1-02 for operational checks after fluid service.
- Refer to SOP-P3-L1-03 for start-up and validation procedures after maintenance.
